description: TWO BUDGETS: the target-system gap is a measured fixture, not a slogan — the oversized estimate and the right-sized one differ by about $2,847/month, and the whole case for a reviewer agent is that a few cents of tokens protects that number
command: python3 -c "import json,sys;a=float(json.load(open('infra/fixtures/cost-estimates/estimate-oversize.json'))['totalMonthlyCost']);b=float(json.load(open('infra/fixtures/cost-estimates/estimate-good.json'))['totalMonthlyCost']);sys.exit(0 if 2800 < (a-b) < 2900 else 1)" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo pass || echo fail

description: TWO BUDGETS: agent-operating cost is tracked separately by YOUR ledger — two budgets with two owners means two artifacts, and a ledger that does not record cost_usd per run cannot own one of them
command: [ -f agentops/ledger.py ] && grep -q 'cost_usd' agentops/ledger.py && echo pass || echo fail

description: TWO BUDGETS: the agent budget has an alert path of its own — budget-check.sh exits non-zero on an over-budget run, so runaway token spend is caught by something other than somebody reading a bill later
